title: Is Sexual Attraction a Gift… or a Test?
paragraphs:
Is Sexual Attraction a Gift… or a Test?
The Desire That Feels Holy… Until It Doesn’t
You didn’t expect it to feel this confusing.
One moment, it feels beautiful. Natural. Even sacred. Your heart beats faster, your mind drifts, your body responds—and somewhere deep inside, you wonder… did God put this here?
And then the next moment… it feels like war.
Because the same attraction that made you feel alive… now makes you feel guilty. Torn. Exposed. Like something inside you is pulling in two directions at once.
And no one really talks about that part.
They tell you “just resist temptation,” but they don’t explain why the desire itself feels so powerful… so human… so close to something good.
So you sit there, quietly asking the question most people are too afraid to say out loud:
Is sexual attraction a gift… or a test?
The truth is… it’s both.
But not in the way you think.
In the beginning, before shame ever entered the human story, before hiding became instinct, before guilt wrapped itself around desire—God created something good.
The Hebrew language doesn’t hide this.
In Genesis 1:27–28, it says:
“וַיִּבְרָא אֱלֹהִים אֶת־הָאָדָם… זָכָר וּנְקֵבָה בָּרָא אֹתָם… וַיְבָרֶךְ אֹתָם אֱלֹהִים… וַיֹּאמֶר לָהֶם פְּרוּ וּרְבוּ”
“Vayivra Elohim et-ha’adam… zakhar u’neqevah bara otam… vayevarekh otam Elohim… vayomer lahem, ‘peru u’revu.’”
God created man… male and female… and He blessed them… and said, “Be fruitful and multiply.”
Do you see it?

Before sin ever existed, attraction had a purpose. It was part of blessing, not brokenness. It wasn’t dirty. It wasn’t shameful. It was sacred… designed to draw two people into covenant, into unity, into something that reflects God’s own creative power.
Even in Genesis 2:25, it says:
“וַיִּהְיוּ שְׁנֵיהֶם עֲרוּמִּים… וְלֹא יִתְבֹּשָׁשׁוּ”
“They were both naked… and were not ashamed.”
No hiding. No confusion. No inner war.
Just purity.
So what happened?
Sin didn’t remove desire.
It distorted it.
Now the same attraction that once pointed toward covenant… can pull toward compromise. The same desire meant to unite… can now divide your soul.
James 1:14–15 reveals this tension clearly:
“ἕκαστος δὲ πειράζεται ὑπὸ τῆς ἰδίας ἐπιθυμίας… εἶτα ἡ ἐπιθυμία συλλαβοῦσα τίκτει ἁμαρτίαν”
“Each person is tempted when he is lured and enticed by his own desire… then desire, when it has conceived, gives birth to sin.”
Notice that.
Desire itself is not immediately called sin.
It’s what happens next.
It’s what you do with it.
It’s where you allow it to go.
That’s where the test begins.
Sexual attraction is a gift when it draws you toward God’s design.
It becomes a test when it tries to pull you outside of it.
And this is where most people break… not because they’re evil, but because they’re exhausted.
Exhausted from fighting something that feels natural.
Exhausted from hiding struggles no one sees.
Exhausted from pretending they’re stronger than they really are.
But here’s what you need to hear… and feel deep in your bones:
Jesus did not come to shame your struggle.
He came to redeem it.
Even the word for temptation in Greek, “πειρασμός” (peirasmos), carries a deeper meaning—it can mean testing… proving… refining.
Not destroying you.
Refining you.
Because God isn’t trying to expose you as weak.
He’s trying to transform you into someone free.
1 Corinthians 10:13 says:
“No temptation (πειρασμός) has overtaken you except what is common to mankind. And God is faithful; He will not let you be tempted beyond what you can bear…”
Do you understand what that means?
You are not uniquely broken.
You are not alone in this war.
You are not disqualified because you feel desire.
You are being invited into a deeper kind of strength… the kind that doesn’t come from pretending you don’t feel… but from surrendering what you feel to Christ.
Because the real question isn’t “why do I feel this?”
The real question is… “who will I become through this?”
Will you let attraction lead you… or will you let Christ lead you through it?
That’s the difference between bondage… and transformation.
And maybe right now, if you’re honest… there’s something this is exposing.
Something you’ve been hiding.
Something you’ve been justifying.
Something you’ve been quietly losing to.
Be honest.
This hit harder than you expected.
Because this isn’t just content.
This is confrontation… wrapped in grace.
And if this spoke to something real inside you… don’t keep it to yourself.
And if you want to stay close to truth like this… follow.
Not for me.
But because your soul needs consistent light in a world that keeps normalizing darkness.
And if you’re serious about growing deeper in Jesus Christ—not surface-level faith, but real transformation—then take the next step.
Because discipleship isn’t accidental.
It’s intentional.
Not to promote a brand…
But to strengthen a life that refuses to stay lukewarm.
Because glorifying God isn’t just about what you feel.
It’s about what you choose… even when it’s hard.
And maybe that’s what this really is.
Not just a struggle.
Not just a question.
But an invitation.
To let Jesus rewrite the part of your story you thought would always control you.
Because the desire didn’t come to destroy you…
It came to reveal what still needs to be surrendered.
And Jesus is still willing to take it.
